Law 6 makes that a two-owner build, not an ambiguity: harbor_master owns WHO MAY, base owns THE DOOR, and the door calls the owner's gate rather than re-deriving its rule.
children: (a) what-a-crossing-carries — settle actor / boat_id / boat_owner / proven_by for a CC-made crossing. GATING: nothing can be cleared until a crossing can be legally described, so this proves before the parent. HALVED 2026-08-10: this child also said 'and populate MethodRegistry with a production register() call so a crossing does not re-run a proof under the tester'. That half is MOOT — the registry was removed 2026-08-05 and clearance.py reads a seal instead, so there is nothing to populate and no proof re-run to avoid. What is left is four field values, which is an answer, not a build.

(b) the-bootstrap-is-a-named-roster — a readable artifact naming which crossings are exempt and why, so the gate crossing itself into existence is a declared exemption rather than an ordering accident. The trouble's filed_edge asked for exactly this and pointed at the same roster question a-voyage-names-its-ticket is already asking. NARROWED 2026-08-10: the roster is NOT invented here. transitions.py:533 already carries `_EXEMPT_ROSTER: frozenset[str] = frozenset()` — built EMPTY and deliberately structural ('structure ahead of any real entry'), keyed by COMPONENT name, consulted only inside _require_named_ticket. So this child is a composition against an existing holding plus one open question the filed_edge already named: is 'may cross without naming a ticket' the same set as 'may cross without clearance'? If yes, one roster gains a second meaning and must say so; if no, they are two rosters and the edge's warning stands.

(c) refuse-on-missing-or-on-failed — settle whether emit refuses a crossing carrying NO cleared_by, or a crossing whose clearance FAILED. The trouble names this as the ticket's first question; the two are different doors with different bootstrap costs. ||| RETIRED 2026-08-10 BY MEASUREMENT, not by opinion, and the deciding lines are recorded here so nobody re-derives them by opening the same file. THE ANSWER: emit refuses on a MISSING cleared_by, and 'refuse on a FAILED clearance' is NOT STATABLE at this door. Measured at cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py — every refusal in clear() raises at lines 319 (Unauthorized, witness smuggling), 332 (Unauthorized, no standing), 338 (GrantExpired), 348 (Unproven) and 359 (Unresourced), and the single call to emit is line 369. All five precede it, so a failed clearance never arrives at emit to be judged; the docstring states the guarantee outright ('every refusal raises before emit is reached, so a refused move leaves no partial record'). NO SWALLOW-AND-CONTINUE EXISTS on either side of the seam: `grep -n 'except|try:' cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py cairn/tools/base/transitions.py` returns ZERO hits in clearance.py and exactly two in transitions.py, neither on this path — line 324 catches an IllegalTransition raised by the v2 MIGRATION helper and re-calls emit (so every gate still runs), and line 905 catches ScanRefused only to re-raise it LOUDER as BuildGateRed. The child is closed; it is not an open ticket standing for a reader to re-open the same file over.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(clearance-actually-gates) -> [PROVED]

watchme.trigger: fires on any pulse reaching the harbor_master's address, reading the crossing census from the component histories under cairn/ — its own component's register, its own read — from an ERA FLOOR set at arming time (2026-08-10T16:40:00, between this voyage's PROVEME crossing and its PROVED crossing). NARROWED 2026-08-10 at arming, and the narrowing is the build's own finding rather than a softening: this clause said 'any journaled forward crossing'. What the seat actually demands is a forward journaled crossing INTO A REST (not is_summons(target)) — the move that ENTERS proven-space — derived from the grammar, which is exactly what let the exemption roster stay EMPTY. Censusing every forward crossing would red on every BUILDME/PROVEME in the corpus at the probe's own birth: the check going red at the moment its condition is satisfied. A probe watches what the gate DEMANDS. It reports a finding on any of three conditions: (a) a demanded-set crossing landed carrying NEITHER cleared_by NOR a named exemption, which is the gate having been bypassed after it was built and is the sharpest possible signal — no sample floor, because one record already proves it; (b) the ratio of NAMED-EXEMPTION crossings to cleared crossings exceeds one in four over the last 20 demanded crossings, which is the roster quietly growing to cover the fleet — the falsifier's first red, caught while it is still a trend; (c) 20 or more demanded crossings have accumulated since the era floor with clearance never once REFUSING one, which is the hollow-gate signal: a door that has never said no is not yet known to be a door. Each finding carries the offending crossings verbatim with their component, seq and actor, so the consumer never re-derives them.
watchme.enough: when at least 20 post-era demanded crossings have landed, ALL of them carrying cleared_by or a named exemption, the roster NOT covering the fleet, AND clearance has REFUSED at least one real crossing (condition c discharged by evidence rather than by time). CORRECTED 2026-08-10 at arming: the authored clause said only 'all of them carrying cleared_by or a named exemption', under which a corpus whose every crossing took an EXEMPTION would CLEAR this watch at exactly the moment falsifier clause (1) — the roster grown to cover the fleet — was met. That is the check going green for the wrong reason, so the roster clause is now part of enough and the trigger/enough pair is mutually exclusive by construction rather than by luck. THE REFUSAL HALF CANNOT BE SATISFIED TODAY, and this is named rather than faked: every refusal raises before emit writes anything, so it leaves no record at all — which is precisely ticket clearance-leaves-a-trace (cast 2026-07-26, at BUILDME, and unreachable until now because a gate with no callers has no refusals to trace). The probe reports refusals_recorded: 0 with the source it looked at named, so this watch cannot clear until that ticket lands. That is the watch's standing pressure toward the one build that makes its own horizon countable — the direction the two tickets' recorded distinction already names. A refusal manufactured by the seat's own proof teeth is NOT counted: the seal answers 'is the code correct', this watch answers 'did it ever have to be'.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact written against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the crossing census, the exemption roster as read, and the refusal record if one exists.
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — the efficacy question ('did making clearance mandatory actually make crossings authorized?') is a claim about an outcome, and the hypothesize tree is where this system's kills and confirmations are already accumulated.
watchme.consumer: harbor_master, the owner of the authority rung — it is the only component that can act on a finding that its own gate is being bypassed, and Law 6 says the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act, never the probe's.
